question: What the original does when the unit panel's `unitname` box renames a unit: CRenameUnitCommand whole, the panel side (when the name is sent, trimmed, refused, capped, who may), the register of used names, and anything else that renames a unit as far as it bears on the register.

addresses.name: CRenameUnitCommand::CRenameUnitCommand_default
addresses.comment: The prototype constructor RegisterCommandTypes uses (0x887142, after `new 0x80`): the CCommand base (+4 = 0x18D, type id 0x394 `rename_unit` at +0x2C and +0x30, +0x34 = 0xFFFF, +0x36 and +0x38 zero), vftable 0x15C8E5C, the unit reference (+0x3C) emptied - pointer 0, id pair the null id read from 0x1A8CC94/0x1A8CC98, its string empty - and the name (+0x64) empty. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitrename.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x5DD6F0 to the `ret 4` at 0x5DD7E2; the vftable store `mov dword ptr [esi], 0x15c8e5c` at 0x5DD772 is one of findRefs --vftable CRenameUnitCommand's three hits; the only caller is 0x887142 inside RegisterCommandTypes, right after `push 0x80; call new`. Wrong if the vftable at 0x15C8E5C were not CRenameUnitCommand's (the RTTI export says it is).

addresses.name: CRenameUnitCommand::CRenameUnitCommand
addresses.signature: CRenameUnitCommand* __stdcall CRenameUnitCommand::CRenameUnitCommand(CRenameUnitCommand* this, CUnit* unit, Hoi3CString name)
addresses.comment: **A unit's rename, as CUnitView's destructor posts it** - its one caller (0x76DA8B), after `new 0x80`. The CCommand base as the prototype's (type id 0x394 `rename_unit`); the unit reference at +0x3C made from the unit pointer (0x42DD70: pointer, id pair, string); the name at +0x64 copied from the by-value string, which is then freed. Tests nothing. `ret 0x24` (4 + 4 + a 0x1C-byte string). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitrename.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x5DD890 to `ret 0x24` at 0x5DD95A; vftable store at 0x5DD90D; findRefs --callers 0x5DD890 gives exactly one call, 0x76DA8B in CUnitView::~CUnitView, which pushes a 0x1C-byte string copy (sub esp,0x1c), the unit (+0x28) and the new storage. Wrong if 0x42DD70 did not build a reference from a pointer - it is the same call the copy of a CRef uses elsewhere (CRenameSubUnitCommand's constructor has the same shape).

addresses.name: CRenameUnitCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: Slot 6, bare `ret`. Re-resolves the unit from the reference's id pair (+0x40/+0x44: the id table at 0x1A857F4 for a type id up to 0x1268, else 0x1A857F0, through 0xA9DA00; the CUnit is the found CPersistent less 8) into +0x3C, then **CUnit_SetName(unit, the name at +0x64)**, which takes every entry of the unit's old name off its owner's names in use and registers the new one. Then, where the in-game screen's slot 105 answers an object (the order of battle browser, CInGameIdler +0x1360), a reference to the unit is appended to its row_changed_queue (+0x148) - COOBBrowser::QueueRowChanged inlined, with no test of whose unit it is. **It tests nothing**: no owner, no empty name, no unchanged name, no uniqueness. The slot 14 gate (0x5E2DF0, one body folded across 18 unit commands) only asks that the unit resolve, at the post and again in the drain, which is why Execute does not test the pointer before using it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitrename.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Slot 6 of the CRenameUnitCommand table by vtable.py; read whole, 0x5DD960 to `ret` at 0x5DDA9F: `lea edi,[eax-8]` then `add esi,0x64; push esi; call 0x5c48e0` (CUnit_SetName, unit in EDI), then the get-or-create of [0x1A89790], `[eax+0xBE8]` slot 0x1A4/4 = 105 (CInGameIdler slot 105 is `mov eax,[ecx+0x1360]; ret`), and `call 0x44f910` with EDI = result+0x148, a vector push_back of 0x28-byte elements (the divide by 0x66666667 >> 4). Wrong if the drain did not re-ask slot 14 - FINDINGS-commands.md has it at 0xA89844.

addresses.name: CRenameUnitCommand::GetTypeId
addresses.comment: Slot 7: `mov eax, 0x394; ret` - the save token `rename_unit`.
addresses.evidence: Two instructions at 0x5DDAA0; ghidra/saveTokens.json gives 916 (0x394) = rename_unit. Slot 7 by vtable.py. Wrong only if the token table were stale.

addresses.name: CRenameUnitCommand::Clone
addresses.comment: Slot 13: a new 0x80-byte CRenameUnitCommand copied from this one through CRenameUnitCommand_copy - the reference (+0x3C..+0x63) and the name (+0x64); the by-value string argument is only freed. `ret 0x1C`.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x5DDB80 to `ret 0x1c` at 0x5DDBEB: `push 0x80; call new; push eax; mov ecx, esi; call 0x5ddbf0`, then the free of [ebp+8] where [ebp+0x1c] >= 0x10. Slot 13 by vtable.py; same shape as CChangeLawCommand::Clone's record.

addresses.name: CRenameUnitCommand::CRenameUnitCommand_copy
addresses.comment: The copy Clone makes: the CCommand base copied (0x40B530), vftable 0x15C8E5C, the reference's pointer and id pair (+0x3C, +0x40, +0x44) and its string (+0x48), the name (+0x64). `this` is the source and `out` the storage; returns `out`. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x5DDBF0 to `ret 4` at 0x5DDC8B; third vftable store at 0x5DDC1C; one caller, Clone at 0x5DDBBE with ECX the source. Named after CMoveCommand::CMoveCommand_copy.

addresses.name: CUnitView::~CUnitView
addresses.comment: **Where a unit is renamed from the interface.** Its one caller is slot 0 (0x36A180). In order: this row taken off the screen's kept-rows list (+0x17C, CList_RemoveNode; the list's byte +0x10 cleared once it is empty). Where the window (+0x20) exists: the `unitname` edit box's raw text (its layout at box +0x48, slot 19), TrimWhitespace (\n, \t, \r and space off both ends); the unit's name (+0x28, CUnit::GetName); **a rename goes out only where the trimmed text differs from the name (String_Equals, exact bytes, case-sensitive), is not empty, and in_panel (+0x30) is set** - the single panel's header, never a row of several selected. Then a new CRenameUnitCommand(unit, text) is posted through the session (game state +0xBE8, slot 18 GetSession, its +0x38's slot 6), **and CUnit_SetName(unit, text) is called at once, locally** (0x76DB32), before the command has run anywhere. No scenario test (CBrigadeView's destructor tests game state +0xD0C; this does not) and no owner test. Then the window's two releases, the leader panel at +0x34 destroyed (CLeaderAssignmentPanel::Destroy) and freed, the glue and base tables restored and the base destructor 0xA7F830. The unit is the raw pointer +0x28, not re-resolved. `ret 4`. functionStart(0x76DB32) answers 0x76D9D3 - the 0xCC at 0x76D9D2 is the disp8 of `mov ecx, [ebp-0x34]` - while retsBefore(0x76D8C0, 0x76DB32) is empty. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitrename.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x76D8C0 to `ret 4` at 0x76DBF3. It writes the CUnitView vftable 0x15D86FC (findRefs --vftable CUnitView: hits in the constructor and here only); its only caller is 0x76A187 in slot 0. The test is at 0x76DA09..0x76DA1F: `call 0x4173c0` (String_Equals, a@EAX = GetName's result, b@EDX = trimmed); `cmp [ebp-0x40], 0; jle` (the trimmed string's size); `cmp byte [ebx+0x30], al` with AL = 0. The unitname string 0x15D8568 has four references: two in the constructor, one in CUnitView::BuildTooltip (0x76B379) and this one - so nothing else reads the box. A scan for `+0xd0c]` finds none here, in the constructor or in Execute, and finds CBrigadeView's at 0x726BC2 (the positive control).

addresses.name: CUnitView::~CUnitView_scalar_deleting
addresses.comment: Slot 0, the deleting form: CUnitView::~CUnitView and free where bit 0 of flags is set. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Fourteen instructions at 0x76A180..0x76A19F; slot 0 of the CUnitView table by vtable.py. Same shape as CBrigadeView::~CBrigadeView_scalar_deleting.

addresses.name: CUnit::GetName
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of CUnit, inherited by CArmy, CNavy and CAir: `out` = a copy of the name (+0x16C). `ret 4`. Slot 8 beside it is GetShortName.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x5C47A0..0x5C47D0: `add ecx, 0x16c` and the string assign into [ebp+8], returned in EAX. vtable.py --holding 0x5C47A0: CUnit, CArmy, CNavy, CAir, slot 7, one family. CUnit +0x16C is the recorded `name`.

addresses.name: StringHashSet_Find
addresses.comment: **A string set's lookup** - the in-use test of a country's names (CCountry +0x84) among 20 callers. The set is {count +0, bucket count +4, bucket array +8}; hash h = 0, then for each byte (signed) h = (h + c) * 61; bucket = h mod the bucket count; the bucket's nodes are {Hoi3CString*, next}. Answers the first stored string of the same length and the same bytes (MemCompareRegs) - **exact, case-sensitive** - else 0. `ret 4`. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0xA86F70 to the two `ret 4` at 0xA87007 and 0xA87012: the loop `movsx ebx, byte [ecx+edx]; add eax, ebx; inc ecx; imul eax, eax, 0x3d`, `div dword [esi+4]`, `mov eax, [esi+8]; mov ebx, [eax+edx*4]`, then MemCompareRegs on the shorter length with the lengths compared after. Called with EAX = country+0x84 by UnregisterUnitName (0x4CB522).

addresses.name: StringHashSet_Insert
addresses.comment: Puts a new 8-byte node {name, next} at the head of the name's bucket (the hash of StringHashSet_Find) and adds one to the count (+0). **No test that an equal string is already held**, so one name can be in the set several times; no rehash, the bucket count is never changed here. Where the node cannot be allocated the bucket head is set to 0 and the count still raised. `ret 4`. Three callers, RegisterUnitName among them. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0xB4A2E0 to the two `ret 4` at 0xB4A33C and 0xB4A34C: the same hash loop, `div dword [edi+4]`, `push 8; call new`, `[eax] = name; [eax+4] = old head; head = eax; inc dword [edi]`. No call and no compare between the hash and the link, which is the absence of a duplicate test.

addresses.name: StringHashSet_RemoveEntry
addresses.comment: Takes off the node that holds exactly this string pointer - found by hashing the string's bytes into its bucket, then by pointer identity - frees the node (not the string) and lowers the count (+0); false where no node holds it. `ret 4`. Two callers: UnregisterUnitName and 0xB4955B (not read). The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x50F960 to the `ret 4`s at 0x50F9B6, 0x50F9D2, 0x50F9EB: the hash of [edi], `div dword [ebx+4]` with EBX = [ebp+8], the walk `cmp dword [eax], edi`, unlink at head or after the previous node, `call free` on the node, `dec dword [ebx]`. findRefs --callers: 0x4CB531 and 0xB4955B.

addresses.name: RegisterUnitName
addresses.comment: Copies a name into a new 0x1C-byte string and adds it (StringHashSet_Insert, 0xB4A2E0) to **the country's** set of names in use, at CCountry +0x84 (`mov edi, [ebp+8]; add edi, 0x84` at 0x4CB4DC) - which CCountry::MakeUnitName's in-use test (StringHashSet_Find, 0xA86F70, on the country's +0x84) asks. So a name is taken only within its country: two countries may call units the same. **Nothing is tested: a name already held is added again**, so the set can hold one name several times. CConstructUnitCommand::Execute calls it after each name it makes, CConstructSingleUnitCommand's constructor after its one, CCreateNewHQCommand::Execute after the brigade's, CUnit_SetName and CSubUnit_SetName after every name they give. `ret 8`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section K, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitrename.md, section 4.
addresses.revises: signature's `CString* name` to `Hoi3CString* name` (the insert hashes [name+0x10] bytes of a std::string), and the comment adds that duplicates are kept and names the set's two helpers
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x4CB450 to `ret 8` at 0x4CB502: new 0x1C, the string copy (0x401BD0) from [ebp+0xC], then `call 0xb4a2e0` with EDI = country+0x84. StringHashSet_Insert has no duplicate test (its own evidence).

addresses.name: UnregisterUnitName
addresses.comment: The inverse of RegisterUnitName, and more than its inverse: **while** StringHashSet_Find finds a string equal to the name in the country's set (+0x84), that entry is taken off (StringHashSet_RemoveEntry) and its copy freed - so **every** entry of the name goes, however many units, brigades, ships or wings registered it, and CCountry::MakeUnitName may then hand the name out again while another of them still bears it. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitrename.md, section 4.
addresses.revises: signature's `char* name` to `Hoi3CString* name` (StringHashSet_Find reads its +0x10 and +0x14), and the comment says the loop removes every equal entry, not one
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x4CB510 to `ret 4` at 0x4CB577: `lea esi, [eax+0x84]`, `call 0xa86f70` with EAX = esi and the name pushed, then a loop of `push esi; call 0x50f960` (EDI = the found string), free of the string's buffer and of the string, and Find again until it answers 0.

addresses.name: CUnit_SetName
addresses.comment: Gives a unit its name: UnregisterUnitName(the owner's country by +0x128, the old name +0x16C) - which takes every entry of the old name off that country's set - then the name copied into +0x16C and RegisterUnitName(the owner's country, it). **Tests nothing**: an empty name, an unchanged one or one already in use all go through. Where the unit has an avatar (+0x164) and show_unit_names (settings +0xE9) is on, the counter is given the name (CHoiAvatar_SetCounterName, which cuts it to 8 characters), or `???` while intel_level (+0x1F8) is below 5. Where the unit is selected (+4): **the global byte 0x1A855F6 is set to 1**, the in-game screen's Deselect (slot 45) and Select (slot 38) are called on it, and the byte is cleared - so CUnit::OnDeselected and CUnit::OnSelected skip RemoveUnitRow and AddUnitRow and the panel is not rebuilt by a rename. `ret 4`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitrename.md, section 4.
addresses.revises: comment only, and confidence inferred to confirmed (read end to end): adds that nothing is tested, that every entry of the old name leaves the set, and the 0x1A855F6 window around the deselect and reselect - the record elsewhere said that byte has no writer
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x5C48E0 to `ret 4` at 0x5C4B1D: `call 0x4cb510` with EAX = country, ESI = edi+0x16C pushed; the assign (0x401BD0); `call 0x4cb450`; the avatar block; `cmp byte [edi+4], bl; je` then `mov byte [0x1a855f6], 1` at 0x5C49EB, [0xBE8] slot 0xB4/4 = 45 and slot 0x98/4 = 38 each with EDI pushed, `mov byte [0x1a855f6], bl` (BL = 0) at 0x5C4B07. findRefs --address 0x1A855F6 finds four references: these two writes and the two reads at 0x5C0896 (OnSelected) and 0x5C0BAC (OnDeselected).

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::AddUnitRow
addresses.comment: **Slot 34: a selected unit gets a row.** Called by CUnit::OnSelected (0x5C08A5) unless the global byte 0x1A855F6 is set - which only CUnit_SetName does, around its deselect and reselect of a selected unit (0x5C49EB, 0x5C4B07), so a rename rebuilds no row. In order: CloseOrdersView; the chat list (+0x1354) is moved to x 350 keeping its home y (+0x1D52); a CUnitView(unit, this, inPanel 0, the kept-rows list +0x1DE4) is made - the `unitpanel` window, the single panel's header row - and appended to the row list (+0xD20 first, +0xD24 last, +0xD28 count; 0x10-byte nodes {row, prev, next, byte}), so **rows are in the order the units were selected**; unless a box drag is in progress (0x64D850) CInGameIdler_LayoutUnitPanels. With the count now 2: multi_unitpanel shown, the upgrades window closed (0x66B7B0), multiunit_slider (+0x136C) hidden, the window at +0x1360 put away (0x7395E0). With the count 1: the single panel (+0x135C) is given the unit and rebuilt (0x762F40) and placed beside the side menu and the +0x1360 window. Then the reorganise window is closed if up, and `desc` is set to the count, a space, and ARMIES / NAVIES / AIRWINGS by the FIRST row's unit (slot 15 land, else slot 16 naval, else air) - '3 Land Units'. With the count 1 every row's window is hidden. No test that the unit already has a row. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section B.1.
addresses.revises: comment only: '(no writer in .text)' was wrong - CUnit_SetName writes 0x1A855F6 at 0x5C49EB (1) and 0x5C4B07 (0); findRefs --address 0x1A855F6 finds those two and the two known reads
addresses.evidence: findRefs --address 0x1A855F6: four references, 0x5C0896 and 0x5C0BAC (the reads already recorded, the positive control) and 0x5C49ED and 0x5C4B09 inside CUnit_SetName, whose listing shows `mov byte ptr [0x1a855f6], 1` and `mov byte ptr [0x1a855f6], bl` with EBX zeroed at 0x5C4930.

addresses.name: CTextLayout::InsertText
addresses.comment: Slot 21. A one-byte string whose byte is on the layout's refused list (+0x88; CTextLayout_RefuseDoubleQuote) does nothing. Otherwise by where the caret stands: at the end of the text CTextLayout_InsertAtEnd, at (0, 0) CTextLayout_InsertAtStart (column = the string's length), else CTextLayout_InsertAtCaret - **each of the three inserts nothing once the text already holds `max length` (+0xA0) bytes or more**, and inserts the whole string otherwise. The caret goes after what was inserted; the line count (+0x40) is rebuilt (GetLastRow + 1, the wrap's breaks counted). **Then, where +0x9A is clear and the area height (+0x4A) is not 0, Backspace (slot 39) runs again and again while (lines - 1) > height / the font's line height (font slot 11), in doubles, or max lines (+0x9C) is not -1 and lines > max lines.** +0x9A is set by the layout's constructor but **every edit box's constructor clears it** (0xA8F528, the layout being at box +0x48), so this runs in every edit box: there, text that would wrap past the box's height - or past one line in `unitname`, whose CUnitView constructor sets max lines 1 - is backspaced off as it is typed. Then every listener's slot 2. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitrename.md, section 5.
addresses.revises: comment only: it said '+0x9A is set by default, so not in an edit box' - the edit box constructor clears +0x9A (box +0xE2) at 0xA8F528, so the fit loop runs in every edit box; the loop's two conditions are now written out
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0xACC600 to `ret 4` at 0xACC7E6: 0xACC73A `cmp byte [esi+0x9a], 0; jne` past the loop, 0xACC748 `cmp word [esi+0x4a], 0; jbe` past it, the loop 0xACC750..0xACC7C4 (cvtsi2ss of lines-1, cvtsi2sd of +0x4A, font [esi+0x78] slot 0x2C/4, divsd, comisd/ja; `[esi+0x9c]` against -1 and against +0x40; `call [edx+0x9c]`, slot 39). The edit box constructor: `xor ebx, ebx` at 0xA8F1AD with no later write to EBX before `mov byte ptr [esi+0xe2], bl` at 0xA8F528, and ESI is the box there (its `mov [esi+0xe8], 0xfa` is the recorded max length 250 at layout +0xA0).

addresses.name: CUnitView::CUnitView
addresses.no_signature: a constructor: the object, the unit and the screen arrive in a mix of ECX, another register and the stack that was read only at its one call site, in CSingleUnitPanel::Rebuild
addresses.comment: **The header row of a unit**: the window `unitpanel`, made both as the second entry of a selected unit's panel (fourth argument 1) and as a row of the list of several selected units (0, from CInGameIdler slot 34). Sets what does not change: the edit box `unitname`, `exp_force`, `counter_type` (the sprite `GFX_counter_` + the first brigade's type, where the player's intel is 3 or more), `counter_size` (frame by oob_level: theatre 6, army group 5, army 4, corps 3, a division 2 with more than one brigade and 1 otherwise), `leader_types`; registers the three buttons. **`unitname`, in order** (0x769D40..0x769E4D): its layout's SetText(CUnit::GetName), EditBox_RefreshText, max lines (layout +0x9C, box +0xE4) = 1, CTextLayout_RefuseDoubleQuote, CaretToTextStart (layout slot 36), EditBox_RefreshText, and read-only (box +0x159 = 1) where in_panel is clear. No scenario test, no owner test, no listener: nothing is told when Enter is pressed, and the box is never filled again. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md, section 4, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitrename.md, section 3. **The leader glue, 2026-10-11**: `leader_button` and `leader_photo` share the glue at +0x128, its ordinary click CUnitView::OnLeaderButton (0x76E2E0) and another event 0x76E3F0. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderwindow.md, section 1.
addresses.revises: comment only: adds the `unitname` steps in order, with the one-line cap and the absence of a scenario test and of a listener
addresses.evidence: The listing 0x769D40..0x769E4D: FindChild('unitname') (window slot 16), unit slot 7 (CUnit::GetName), `[ecx+0x48]` slot 0x40/4 = 16 (SetText), `call 0xa90140`, `mov dword ptr [esi+0xe4], 1`, `call 0xaccfe0` with ESI = box+0x48, slot 0x90/4 = 36, `call 0xa90140`, then `cmp byte [edi+0x30], bl; jne` around `mov byte ptr [eax+0x159], 1`. The same grep for `0xe4], 1` over CBrigadeView::CBrigadeView finds no store (the brigade card's box has no line cap).

structs.name: CRenameUnitCommand
structs.comment: The command that renames a unit (type id 0x394, `rename_unit`; keys `unit` and `name`). 0x80 bytes, the size every `new` for it asks. Posted only by CUnitView::~CUnitView. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitrename.md, section 1.
structs.evidence: `push 0x80; call new` before both the constructor (0x76DA4A) and the prototype constructor (0x887126), and in Clone (0x5DDB9C); the copy constructor writes nothing past +0x7C (the name string's capacity). vftable 0x15C8E5C (VA) by findRefs --vftable; RTTI parent CCommand.

struct_fields.name: unit
struct_fields.comment: The unit, as a 0x28-byte reference: the cached CUnit* (+0x3C), its id pair (+0x40 type, +0x44 id) and a string (+0x48). ParseObjectReference fills it from the `unit` key; IsValid (slot 14) and Execute re-resolve the pointer from the pair.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's `unit` case `lea esi, [ecx+0x3c]; call 0x5ec150` (ParseObjectReference); the constructor's 0x42DD70 into +0x3C; Execute and slot 14 read +0x40/+0x44 and write the resolved pointer to +0x3C; the copy constructor copies +0x3C, +0x40, +0x44 and the string at +0x48.

struct_fields.name: name
struct_fields.comment: The new name, as given - CUnitView's destructor hands it already trimmed. The `name` key; Execute passes it to CUnit_SetName.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's `name` case assigns the parse buffer (parse +0x22C) to this+0x64; the constructor copies its by-value string to +0x64; Execute does `add esi, 0x64; push esi; call 0x5c48e0`; the base destructor 0x5DD820 frees +0x64 (capacity at +0x78).

struct_fields.name: unit_names_in_use
struct_fields.comment: **The count of a string set held here by value**, the names the country's units, brigades, ships and wings bear: count +0x84, bucket count +0x88, bucket array +0x8C (nodes {Hoi3CString*, next}). RegisterUnitName adds to it (StringHashSet_Insert, which keeps duplicates), UnregisterUnitName takes every equal entry off it, CCountry::MakeUnitName asks it (StringHashSet_Find, exact and case-sensitive). A name is taken only within its country. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section K, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitrename.md, section 4.
struct_fields.revises: type void* to int and the comment: the set is embedded at +0x84 (`lea esi, [eax+0x84]`), +0x84 being its count; the container's layout, which the comment said was not read, is now read
struct_fields.evidence: UnregisterUnitName `lea esi, [eax+0x84]` and passes ESI as the set; the set's +0 is `inc`/`dec`ed by StringHashSet_Insert/RemoveEntry, its +4 is the divisor of the hash, its +8 the bucket array. CCountry +0x90 is nukes, so the set is exactly 0xC bytes.

struct_fields.name: unit_names_bucket_count
struct_fields.comment: The bucket count of the names-in-use set at +0x84: the divisor of the name's hash. Never changed by the insert. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitrename.md, section 4.
struct_fields.evidence: `div dword ptr [esi+4]` in StringHashSet_Find with ESI = country+0x84, the same in StringHashSet_Insert and RemoveEntry.

struct_fields.name: unit_names_buckets
struct_fields.comment: The bucket array of the names-in-use set at +0x84: one head pointer per bucket, each a chain of 8-byte nodes {Hoi3CString*, next}. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitrename.md, section 4.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov eax, [esi+8]; mov ebx, [eax+edx*4]` in StringHashSet_Find; the insert links its node at `[edi+8] + bucket*4`.

slots_noted: CRenameUnitCommand slot 14 (0x5E2DF0, IsValid: resolve the unit from +0x40/+0x44 into +0x3C, true where found) is one body in 18 unit-command tables, so it is left unnamed. Slot 0 (0x5DD7F0) and the base destructor it calls (0x5DD820, frees +0x64, +0x48 and the CCommand name) are shared with CRenameSubUnitCommand, the two classes having one layout; left unrecorded. Slots 2 and 4 are the generated SaveContents and the recorded LoadKey.
